signs: Elevated REL/WME readings at base tapering off at ~1-1.2m; Visual tide marks; White salt efflorescence; Intact continuous horizontal mortar joints.
notes: Prefer chemical DPC where there is a continuous horizontal mortar course. Prefer Electro Osmosis (not chemical DPC) for random rubble, stonework, poured mass concrete, walls lacking a continuous mortar course, or masonry above timber joists. Both replaster and plasterboard may be suggested; surveyor chooses. Suggest annual monitoring after major rising-damp works.

signs: Elevated RH (>55-60%); Wall surface temp < calculated Dew point; Black mould (Aspergillus) on external walls/ceilings/reveals; Superficial moisture meter readings.
notes: Prefer PIV for whole-house atmospheric moisture; prefer HRV when energy-efficient pre-warming of winter intake air is needed; prefer 100mm single-room ventilation when mould/condensation is isolated to one room (kitchen/utility) and whole-house PIV is not warranted. Suggest ozonation as the final mould-remediation phase where contamination or odours are severe. Isotherm vs wall insulation investigation — pick what the notes support. Locations useful for mould treatment and bathroom fans.

signs: Elevated moisture readings at random, localized heights; Blown/cracked exterior render; Defective mortar pointing; Blocked gutters/downpipes; Ivy growth; Porous brickwork; Damp beside windows/doors; Cavity bridging.
notes: Consultation / third-party only — do not invent DampMaster billed costs for external repairs. Prefer water-repellent coatings for porous facade / wind-driven rain; seal openings when damp is adjacent to fenestrations; clear cavity when cavity-wall bridging/debris is indicated.

signs: Highly localized elevated moisture (e.g., under bath, sink, radiator); No corresponding external architectural defects.
Disused, sealed fireplace; Damp soot staining on internal chimney breast plaster.
notes: Core drill adapted for vent installation — location = chimney breast / room.

signs: Below-ground masonry (cellar/basement/retaining wall); High lateral hydrostatic pressure; Seeping water; High water table (BS 8102 Grade 3 environment).
notes: Locations for basement/cellar walls and floors. Prefer leak sealing resin injection for active leaks in waterproof concrete structures such as lift pits, car parks, and plant rooms (Type B/C) where drainage systems are impractical.

signs: External ground level higher than internal floor level; Water pooling at base of exterior walls; Hardstanding sloping toward masonry.
Deep cuboidal cracking across timber grain; White/grey mycelium; Rust-red spore dust; Fleshy fruiting bodies; Timber moisture >28%.
notes: Location = subfloor / affected voids. Prefer environmental treatment where chemical irrigation is unsuitable (e.g. historic buildings) and the moisture source is already repaired. Prefer boron rods/preservatives for at-risk timber that is not yet heavily decayed.

signs: Flight holes visible in timber surface; Frass (bore dust) present in attic or subfloor joists.
notes: Location = roof void / attic / joists. Boron as protective follow-on for at-risk timber.

signs: Loft insulation depth measured at <300mm; Insulation heavily compressed into eaves; Visible condensation on roof timbers.
Flooding, burst pipes, or sewage backflow; Standing or saturated water; Urgent need for forced drying; Risk of rapid mould growth after water ingress.
notes: Prefer commercial flood drying equipment for Class 1–4 water damage. Ozonation/mould treatment when contamination or odours develop after wetting.
